findings.title: r-efi 6.0.0 AUTHORS contains the MIT grant; the notice says the crate has no MIT text
findings.evidence: static.crates.io r-efi-6.0.0.crate sha256 f8dcc9c7d52a811697d2151c701e0d08956f92b0e24136cf4cf27b57a6a0d9bf matches b2 Cargo.lock. No file named LICENSE, COPYING, or NOTICE. README.md sha256 420f65fec3ba2e89d49da51b222d2881d26959037a7b7d3794143db4bd4627b1 names the SPDX expression in markdown and does not contain the MIT grant. AUTHORS sha256 d027e91dbc9cdbb2f1190068e498bd6b61cff022b6a032b191021ba658d96111 matches the commit provenance and contains the MIT permission text under AUTHORS-MIT, then copyright lines for Red Hat 2017-2023, Microsoft 2019-2023, and David Rheinsberg 2022-2023, then an authors list. AUTHORS-ASL and AUTHORS-LGPL are pointers, not the full Apache-2.0 or LGPL texts. The copyright lines are below the grant. r-efi 5.3.0 README is byte-identical; its AUTHORS sha256 ff92bed461f50338dd703a9ba9aee496a425957873df1d91192776e4bdf5dda7 begins with the same MIT grant. The synthetic missing-text fixture still exits 0 and is a different tree.
findings.required_change: Rewrite the r-efi sentences so they describe AUTHORS-MIT, the copyright lines, the author list, and the Apache and LGPL pointers. Keep the filename fact. Do not call the missing-text fixture the r-efi fact. Leave the ISC allow entry in place.
